## Natural history notes

A large orbweaver characterized by a rounded abdomen, spiny-looking legs, and highly variable coloration ranging from brown and orange to gray or pale tan, often with mottled markings that help it blend into bark and leaves. In Florida, the Tropical Orbweaver is common in gardens, yards, hammocks, forest edges, parks, citrus groves, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats. It builds large circular webs at night to capture moths, flies, beetles, mosquitoes, and other flying insects, often hiding during the day in folded leaves, bark crevices, or nearby shelter.
